---
title: "Open Science in the Swedish Context 2026"
---

<br>

## Course Overview

<div class="lesson-overview">

<p><span class="fa-regular fa-bookmark"></span> <strong>Description</strong><br>
This course is designed to equip academics across all disciplines with a range of tools needed to implement Open Science practices into every step of their research project lifecycle. In this interactive, hands-on course, participants will learn about Open Science through interactive lectures, discussions with guest speakers, and practical sessions. <br></p>
<p>Participants will gain knowledge and skills to enable them to implement Open Science practices for: <br></p>
<ul>
  <li>Research planning and experiment design</li>
  <li>Data collection and analysis</li>
  <li>Publishing research results and education resources</li>
  <li>Making research data and other outputs available for re-use</li>
  <li>Communicating your research results to the public and other stakeholders</li>
</ul>

<p><span class="fa-solid fa-arrow-left"></span> <strong>Prerequisites</strong><br>
To follow this course, learners should have basic knowledge of:<br>
1. Principles of scientific research and methodology<br>
2. How research outputs are typically disseminated, (e.g., journals, conferences etc.)<br>
3. The structure of the Swedish research system, including universities and funding bodies. 
</p>

<p><span class="fa-solid fa-arrow-right"></span> <strong>Learning Outcomes</strong><br>
1. Explain what Open Science is. Discuss the benefits and challenges that come with its implementation, specifically in the Swedish context<br>
2. Describe the most common Open Science practices throughout every step of the research project lifecycle<br>
3. Implement Open Science practices into their own workflow</p>

<p><span class="fa-solid fa-users"></span> <strong>Target Audience:</strong> PhD students, postdocs, researchers, PIs and other employees at all Swedish universities</p>

<p><span class="fa-solid fa-unlock"></span> <strong>License:</strong> All course material will be made available 
<a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/">CC BY 4.0</a> following the conclusion of the course.</p>

</div>
